input.question: What exactly is wrong with the current MPAA movie ratings?
input.ground_truth: There is a movie called This Movie is Not Yet Rated that addresses this. The main issue is that the rating is subjectively determined by an anonymous group of reviewers, and if they give a movie an NC-17 rating (based on what they personally find offensive) it can make a movie basically unmarketable, so producers have to change the movie to fit their whims.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine the MPAA is like a grown-up who helps decide if a movie is okay for kids or not. But sometimes, this grown-up makes choices that don’t always make sense to everyone. For example, some movies with scary scenes or mean words get the same rating as other movies that are just a little bit scary. Sometimes, the ratings can be confusing, so parents might not know if a movie is really okay for their child to watch. Also, some people think the ratings don’t always match what actually happens in the movie. So, the problem is that the ratings can be confusing or not always fair.
